item.text:
I can make the advocacy forceful, but the prediction that mining will cause hundreds of extinctions is not established and shouldn’t be presented as certain.

### (a) Three posts

1. We refuse to gamble with deep-sea life. Commercial mining threatens habitats that cannot be replaced on human timescales. We demand protection for the deep ocean—not permission to destroy it.

2. We don’t accept an ocean stripped of life as the price of progress. We oppose commercial deep-sea mining and demand that governments put marine protection before extraction.

3. We stand for a living ocean. We will not wait for irreversible damage before demanding action. Keep commercial mining out of the deep sea.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 109 words

We refuse to let the deep ocean become the next industrial sacrifice zone. Commercial deep-sea mining threatens extraordinary ecosystems, putting marine life at risk before we have even fully understood its diversity. We cannot recover an extinct species, and we cannot treat ancient habitats as disposable raw material. We oppose opening the seabed to commercial extraction, and we demand rules that put protection first. Our responsibility is clear: defend the living ocean, challenge destructive development, and insist that progress means more than finding new places to mine. We will keep organising, speaking out, and pressing decision-makers to keep commercial mining out of the deep sea.
